summary: Defines a MIB module for managing VDSL2 interfaces, which are also relevant for related line types.

eli5.summary: VDSL2 is a fast internet-over-phone-line technology. This gives gauges to check on its lines.

questions: what is a vdsl2 configuration template
how does snmp manage dsl lines
subtitle: An SNMP management model for VDSL2 lines, and for ADSL, ADSL2 and ADSL2+ lines too.

tldr.problem: Operators of DSL access equipment needed one standard way to configure, monitor and test VDSL2 lines, and the existing ADSL MIB modules could not describe VDSL2.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 5650 defines the VDSL2-LINE-MIB module with tables for line configuration, status, performance counters and notifications. Settings are shared through profiles and templates, and the module is selected by the interface type 251.
tldr.outcome: A line reporting ifType vdsl2(251) must be managed with this MIB. The older ADSL MIB modules (RFC 2662 and RFC 4706) are not obsoleted.

today: RFC 5650 is a Proposed Standard, and the metadata shows no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It is meant to sit alongside RFC 2662 and RFC 4706, which it does not obsolete.

sections.title: What the VDSL2 MIB Covers
sections.content:
RFC 5650 defines a Management Information Base (MIB) module for VDSL2 interfaces. Objects in a MIB are normally read and written with the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) and are described using SMIv2, the Structure of Management Information.

The same module also manages ADSL, ADSL2 and ADSL2+ lines. VDSL2 itself is defined by ITU-T G.993.2, and the model follows the physical layer management standard ITU-T G.997.1 and the DSL Forum framework TR-129.

The RFC is long, about 218 pages, and most of that is the formal MIB module in section 3. The prose sections explain how the module is organised.
sections.eli5: It is a giant control panel for phone-line internet. Each dial or gauge on the panel has a name, and the document lists them all.

sections.title: Choosing Between the DSL MIB Modules
sections.content:
This RFC does not obsolete RFC 2662 (ADSL lines) or RFC 4706 (ADSL2 and ADSL2+). Instead the interface type reported in the IF-MIB decides which module applies.

  • ADSL lines with ifType=adsl(94) MUST be managed with RFC 2662.
  • ADSL, ADSL2 and ADSL2+ lines with ifType=adsl2plus(238) MUST be managed with RFC 4706.
  • VDSL2, ADSL, ADSL2 and ADSL2+ lines with ifType=vdsl2(251) MUST be managed with this document.

The first-generation VDSL standard, G.993.1, is not covered. Those lines MUST be managed with RFC 3728. The RFC also notes that this MIB assumes a more sophisticated management model than older modems, even ADSL2 ones, may support.
sections.eli5: There are three different control panels for three generations of phone-line internet. A line tells you which kind it is, and you must use the matching panel.

sections.title: Fitting Into IF-MIB and Line Topology
sections.content:
The module hooks into the Interfaces MIB of RFC 2863. Objects such as ifIndex, ifDescr and ifOperStatus are not duplicated. ifPhysAddress MUST be an octet string of zero length, and the ifFixedLengthGroup MUST be supported. A channel may use ifType interleave(124), fast(125) or channel(70).

Configuration lives in profile tables tied to the physical-layer interface only. The ifStackTable links each channel interface, and any higher layer such as ATM, down to that physical entry so its settings can be found.

A line has two units, a central office unit (atuc or vtuc) and a remote unit (atur or vtur). Up to 4 channels can run over the line, each carrying an independent information flow, depending on the technology. Support for the Entity MIB of RFC 4133 is optional.
sections.eli5: Think of one phone wire carrying up to four separate lanes of traffic between the phone company's box and your home box. Each lane gets its own entry in the lists.

sections.title: Tables and Groups
sections.content:
The module is split into groups of tables:

  • Line configuration, maintenance and status: xdsl2LineTable, xdsl2LineSegmentTable and xdsl2LineBandTable.
  • Channel status: xdsl2ChannelStatusTable.
  • Subcarrier status: mostly results of a Dual Ended Loop Test (DELT), in xdsl2SCStatusTable and two companion tables.
  • Unit inventory: xdsl2LineInventoryTable, read through the embedded operations channel (EOC).
  • Performance: current, 15-minute history and 1-day history tables at line, initialization and channel level.
  • Configuration and alarm profiles and templates.
  • Notifications.

The RFC lists many textual conventions in a companion VDSL2-LINE-TC-MIB, such as Xdsl2Unit, Xdsl2Direction and Xdsl2RaMode. Many status values for the remote unit come over the EOC, so they may be unavailable if it cannot be reached during a line error.
sections.eli5: The control panel is split into drawers: one for settings, one for current readings, one for the line's history, and one for alarms.

sections.title: Profiles and Templates
sections.content:
A managed node may handle hundreds or thousands of lines, and most are provisioned identically. So the MIB uses profiles and templates. A line configuration profile holds line-level settings such as the enabled xDSL modes, power spectrum, rate adaptation and SNR margin. A channel configuration profile holds service-level settings such as minimum and maximum data rates and impulse noise protection. A configuration template is a profile of profiles: one line profile plus one to four channel profiles.

Alarm thresholds work the same way, with line alarm profiles, channel alarm profiles and alarm templates. Profiles and templates are named with SnmpAdminString values, and many lines can point at one template, for example one named silver.

Implementations MUST provide a default profile and template called DEFVAL, used automatically before a line's templates are set. A template MUST be unreferenced from all lines before it is deleted, and a profile from all templates.

Changes to a profile or template in use MUST take effect immediately and MAY restart the line's units. A network element MAY also implement a fallback template, tried if the line fails with the primary one, with the xTU-C alternating between them until one works. The number of bearer channels is set by which channel profiles a template names, and the agent creates or destroys channel rows to match.
sections.eli5: Instead of setting every line by hand, you make a recipe card, like 'silver plan', and tell many lines to follow it. Change the card and they all change.

sections.title: Counters, Buckets and Thresholds
sections.content:
Counters apply at three levels. On the whole line there are counters for full and short initializations and their failures. On each transceiver unit there are counters for LOS seconds, errored seconds (ES), severely errored seconds (SES), FEC seconds and unavailable seconds (UAS). On each bearer channel there are counters for coding violations (CRC anomalies) and corrected blocks.

Each counter has a current 15-minute bucket, 0 to 96 history buckets of 15 minutes, a current 1-day bucket and 0 to 30 previous 1-day buckets. Implementations SHOULD support at least 16 of the 15-minute buckets and at least 1 previous day. Counters are not reset when a transceiver is reinitialized, only when the agent is reset or reinitialized.

If data for an interval is suspect, the agent MUST report it as invalid and MUST NOT send notifications based on it. A bucket can still be reported valid with its actual monitoring time in seconds, for example after a clock adjustment.
sections.eli5: The line keeps a tally of its mistakes in short and long notebooks, one page per 15 minutes and one per day. If a page looks unreliable, it says so.

sections.title: Notifications and Line Tests
sections.content:
Agents are required to be able to generate coldStart and warmStart (per agent) and linkUp and linkDown (per interface). A linkDown MAY be sent when ES, SES, CRC anomaly, LOS, LOF or UAS events occur, and the linkUp MAY follow when all failure conditions clear.

The module's own notifications cover status changes and threshold crossings for full and short initialization failures, ES, SES, LOS seconds, UAS, FEC seconds, FEC events and CRC anomalies. Each threshold has its own value, and a value of 0 disables that notification. Two status objects hold bitmasks of outstanding error conditions for the remote and central units.

Writable command objects on xdsl2LineTable can force power management states (xdsl2LineCmndConfPmsf), start a loop diagnostic (xdsl2LineCmndConfLdsf) whose results land in the subcarrier status tables, or request a bits-per-subcarrier measurement (xdsl2LineCmndConfBpsc). The agent should allow only one such measurement at a time.
sections.eli5: When too many mistakes pile up, the line rings a bell. You can also ask the line to run a self-check and write down the results.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Many objects are read-write or read-create, and the RFC walks through them table by table. Unauthorized changes to a template object could have a major adverse effect on many lines at once. Changes to xdsl2LineCmndConfLdsf could trigger an unscheduled line test, and changes to xdsl2LineCmndConfReset could cause an unscheduled retrain of a line.

Some readable objects are sensitive too. The inventory table reveals which vendor's equipment is in use, which can matter for competitive reasons.

SNMP versions before SNMPv3 did not include adequate security. The RFC recommends deploying SNMPv3 with its cryptographic authentication and privacy, and configuring access so only principals with legitimate rights can read or change the objects.
sections.eli5: Anyone who can flip these switches could mess up many lines at once, so only trusted people should get the key, and the messages should be locked.

sections.title: Notes for Managing ADSL With This MIB
sections.content: A management application built for RFC 2662 must adapt to differences before using this module on ADSL links. Templates can name 1 to 4 channels, but ADSL links are limited to two at most. Impulse noise protection is given by minimum protection and maximum delay parameters. The line profile has a sub-table of mode-specific parameters, and for ADSL the application SHOULD create a row for the ADSL modes only. Many parameters and status objects are irrelevant for some ADSL modes, so the RFC advises consulting ITU-T G.997.1.
sections.eli5: If you used the old ADSL control panel, the new one has extra dials. Some of them do nothing on older lines, so you ignore those.
